findings.evidence: Parameters.lean:306-309 `@[simp] theorem chiralCoupling_isospin_zero ... = -(q * s2)`; Parameters.lean:346-350 `@[simp] theorem ofQuantumNumbers_gR ... = chiralCoupling 0 q s2`; Parameters.lean:355-358 `eq_ofQuantumNumbers_iff ... ∧ c.gR = chiralCoupling 0 q s2`.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` from `chiralCoupling_isospin_zero`, keeping `chiralCoupling 0 q s2` as the normal form used by `ofQuantumNumbers_gR` and `eq_ofQuantumNumbers_iff`; alternatively state `ofQuantumNumbers_gR` (and the second conjunct of `eq_ofQuantumNumbers_iff`) with `-(q * s2)` directly. Pick one normal form.
findings.issue: `chiralCoupling_isospin_zero` is `@[simp]` (`chiralCoupling 0 q s2 = -(q * s2)`), while `ofQuantumNumbers_gR` (line 347) is `@[simp]` with RHS `chiralCoupling 0 q s2`. The simp normal form of `(ofQuantumNumbers t3 q s2).gR` is therefore `-(q * s2)`, so `ofQuantumNumbers_gR`'s RHS is not normal and `simp` erases the `chiralCoupling 0 q s2` in which `eq_ofQuantumNumbers_iff` (line 355) states the right-handed half of the characterisation — the named notion never survives in a simp-normal goal.

findings.evidence: Parameters.lean:30 `@[expose] public section`; Parameters.lean:370 `def smTreeLevelCouplings`; Parameters.lean:404,410,435,479 `simp only [..., smTreeLevelCouplings]`. `grep smTreeLevelCouplings` shows the only other user is Couplings.lean, which already goes through the new lemmas (Couplings.lean:81,91,101), so no out-of-file use depends on the body.
findings.fix: Mark `smTreeLevelCouplings` `@[no_expose]` and route `c1Up_eq_two_mul_gA_mul_gV` (404), `c1Down_eq_two_mul_gA_mul_gV` (410), `electronWeakCharge_eq_four_mul_gA_mul_gV` (435) and `electron_gV_eq_zero_iff` (479) through the new `smTreeLevelCouplings_*` lemmas.
findings.issue: `smTreeLevelCouplings` is under the file's `@[expose] public section`, so its body stays part of the public surface even though this PR adds the three projection lemmas (`smTreeLevelCouplings_electron/_upType/_downType`) that make unfolding unnecessary; four in-file proofs still unfold the raw definition with `simp only [smTreeLevelCouplings]`. The PR marks its own four new defs `@[no_expose]`, so the body should not remain exposed here for want of nothing.

summary: The new coupling API is well-formed (bodies `@[no_expose]`, `_def` lemmas via `(rfl)`, `eq_ofQuantumNumbers_iff` characterisation), but two annotation/exposure items need fixing: `chiralCoupling_isospin_zero` as `@[simp]` destroys the normal form that `ofQuantumNumbers_gR` and `eq_ofQuantumNumbers_iff` are stated in, and `smTreeLevelCouplings` keeps an exposed body although this PR adds exactly the projection lemmas that remove the need for it.
